title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples

epigraph.quote: A defense board is not just copper and chips. It is a real-time system where failure puts national safety at risk.
epigraph.author: Mujahid Alam, CEO, Mistral Solutions

web_blocks.html: Because Akkodis is buying the legacy staffing units, we must separate past total sales (₹1,159 Cr in FY26) from the continuing hardware core [1]. In Q1 FY27 (ended June 30, 2026), continuing sales jumped 94% YoY to ₹183.4 Cr [2]. Gross sales including exited services reached ₹346.7 Cr in that quarter [2]. Going forward, AXISCADES focuses on four main segments [3].

web_blocks.html: Let us walk through four real product examples [4]. This shows the buyer's problem, what AXISCADES builds, and how the firm makes money [4].

Segment 1: Defense Electronics (Mistral Solutions). This unit holds the strongest moat [5]. Mistral designs rugged boards, fast FPGA cards, and defense boxes tested from -40°C to +85°C [6]. It holds ~₹100 Cr in orders for Signal and Data Processing Units (SDPUs) on DRDO's Ashwini radar [7]. It also builds upgrade electronics for Sukhoi Su-30MKI jets [7].

Q1 FY27 figures already show how fast the revenue mix is shifting toward core hardware [2]. While exited staffing groups brought ₹163.3 Cr of transitional sales in the quarter, the core hardware arm posted ₹183.4 Cr (+94% YoY) [2]. Inside Mistral, product teams work across four steady defense lines: radar signal cards, telemetry pods, electronic warfare kits, and anti-drone shields [6, 7]. Adding Cloud Wave and ITSJ connects that design work to 5-axis metal milling and cold-plate assembly [11]. Instead of stopping at circuit drawings, AXISCADES can now build, seal, test, and ship full rugged boxes under one roof [11].

web_blocks.title: CONCRETE EXAMPLE 1: Forward Base AI Counter-Unmanned Aerial System (C-UAS)
paragraphs: Problem: Forward Army bases face small suicide drones flying under 100 meters. Big long-range air radars often miss them in ground clutter.

Solution: Mistral builds mobile AI Counter-UAS domes. A 3D MIMO radar spots rotor blades up to 5 km away. An RF sensor tracks drone links at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz. Then a thermal camera locks on and AI splits drones from birds in under two seconds before smart jammers cut the flight link.
Economics: Each system sells for ₹3.5 Cr to ₹7.5 Cr. Bought sensors cost ~55%, leaving ~45% gross margin on AI software, build work, and maintenance contracts.

web_blocks.html: Segment 2: Aerospace Systems & Tooling. Pure staffing moves into the 51%/49% Akkodis deal [8]. AXISCADES keeps aero manufacturing, tooling, wire harnesses, and Devanahalli Aero Land MRO hubs [8]. Its teams bring over 15 years of work on Airbus airframe projects in Toulouse and Hamburg [9].

web_blocks.title: CONCRETE EXAMPLE 2: Commercial Narrowbody Floor-Grid & Cabin Structural Retrofit
paragraphs: Problem: An airline wants more seats and moved galleys inside an Airbus A321neo cabin. Changing seat tracks shifts weight balance and needs full EASA and FAA recertification.

Solution: Engineers take digital plane files and run stress solvers under 16g crash loads. They design light metal brackets that keep safety margins above 1.25 while cutting extra weight. Certified leads then file the stress proof.
Economics: Fixed kits run 9 to 14 months at $750k to $1.5M each. They earned 14%–18% operating margins before the Akkodis sale.

web_blocks.html: Segment 3: Precision Machining & AI Cooling (Cloud Wave + XiDA). AXISCADES is building a physical parts arm under 'Power 930' [10]. Cloud Wave (₹260 Cr EV) brings 5-axis CNC machining and 3D metal parts in Bengaluru [11]. In Silicon Valley, US arm XiDA bought ITSJ Group (~$7M) to serve AI data center cooling and chip tools [11].

web_blocks.title: CONCRETE EXAMPLE 3: Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling Cold Plate for 1,000W+ AI Server Racks
paragraphs: Problem: Big AI server chips burn 700W to 1,200W of heat in a tiny spot. Air fans cannot cool these hot racks fast enough.

Solution: XiDA designs and Cloud Wave mills copper cold plates with 50-micron fluid channels. Surface flatness stays within 5 microns to pull heat off the chip. Helium tests at 150 psi check for zero leaks before delivery.
Economics: Full rack cooling kits sell for $12,000 to $18,000 per rack. High machine precision and leak testing support 18%–22% EBITDA margins at scale.

web_blocks.html: Segment 4: Space Subsystems (Xponential Space). Low Earth Orbit satellites need light, strong frames [12]. Working with partners like U-Space, AXISCADES builds satellite structures, light baffles, and solar deployment links [13].

web_blocks.title: CONCRETE EXAMPLE 4: 150 kg LEO Earth-Observation Satellite Structural Bus
paragraphs: Problem: A 150 kg radar satellite riding an ISRO rocket must survive 12g launch shake and -120°C to +130°C space swings.
Solution: AXISCADES crafts an octagonal carbon-fiber frame over aluminum honeycombs. It uses low-shock release locks so solar wings open gently without shaking delicate optics.
Economics: Flight-ready bus structures sell for ₹2.5 Cr to ₹4.5 Cr each. Cleanroom and vacuum test barriers support 20%+ EBITDA margins.

book_paragraphs: To really understand what AXISCADES builds, you and I have to clear away the outdated labels from five years ago. If you open an old stock screener, it will still describe this company as an engineering design services firm. That description is rapidly becoming obsolete. When AXISCADES struck its mid-2026 deal to divest its traditional aerospace, heavy engineering, and automotive staffing practices to Akkodis, it drew a sharp line in the sand: it no longer wanted to compete solely by renting out engineering hours.

Walk with me instead through what remains and what is scaling. At the heart of the continuing enterprise sits Mistral Solutions, acquired completely in late 2022. Think about what happens when hostile drones carrying explosives fly fifty feet above rugged terrain along India's northern border. Conventional long-range military radars cannot distinguish a plastic quadcopter from a flock of birds. Mistral builds the autonomous Counter-UAS shield that solves that problem: a 3D MIMO radar scans the horizon, radio sensors intercept the pilot's control frequency, thermal cameras lock onto the aircraft, an onboard neural network verifies it is a drone, and directional jamming cuts off its GPS and flight controls within seconds. That is not outsourced drafting; that is proprietary defense hardware.

Alongside counter-drone systems, Mistral serves as the computing brain inside India's Ashwini low-level transportable radar, supplying liquid-cooled Signal and Data Processing Units to Bharat Electronics Limited. Simultaneously, AXISCADES is building a physical manufacturing arm across Bengaluru and Silicon Valley. Through the acquisition of Cloud Wave Technologies and US subsidiary XiDA (which absorbed ITSJ Group), the company is milling copper microchannel cold plates to cool next-generation AI data-center chips that generate over a thousand watts of heat on a single silicon die. And through Xponential Space, engineers are assembling structural frames for Low Earth Orbit satellites. By shedding linear service staffing and doubling down on defense electronics, precision CNC machining, and AI thermal hardware, AXISCADES is attempting to move up the value chain from contractor to proprietary product owner.

Vertical integration is the quiet core of this reset. Design teams inside Mistral once sent complex metal housings and cold plates out to third-party machine shops. With Cloud Wave's 5-axis CNC bays in Bengaluru and ITSJ's US liquid-cooling assembly lines, AXISCADES keeps design tolerances and factory margins in-house.

To make the segments concrete, picture a single Indian defense program from first order to final cash. A laboratory such as DRDO designs a radar. A public-sector prime such as BEL builds the complete system. Mistral is a sub-supplier that designs and builds the processing units inside the radar. It spends months on prototypes, then on field trials, then on qualification, and only after acceptance does it invoice.

That chain explains both the strength and the weakness of the segment. The strength is lock-in: once a board is qualified inside a radar, the buyer does not casually swap it. The weakness is timing: revenue arrives in lumps, and cash arrives later still. The company must fund months of work from its own balance sheet before it can bill.

The newer segments follow a different rhythm. Precision machining and AI cooling plates sell to commercial customers with shorter cycles and faster payment, but they face more competition and tighter pricing. Space structures sit between the two, with long qualification and a small number of buyers. A balanced reading holds all four rhythms in mind at once, rather than assuming the whole company behaves like its best segment.

book_callouts.title: THE FLIGHT QUALIFICATION BARRIER
book_callouts.quote: In aerospace and defense, software bugs cause reboots; structural or electronic failures cause catastrophic loss.
book_callouts.text: Every hardware system shipped across Mistral, Cloud Wave, and Xponential Space must survive brutal environmental qualification tests before entering active duty. Components endure MIL-STD-810G thermal shock (-55°C to +125°C), MIL-STD-461E electromagnetic interference shielding, and random vibration shake tables.
bullets: AS9100 Rev D aerospace manufacturing quality certification.
CEMILAC and DGQA military airworthiness approvals for airborne boxes.
Helium mass-spectrometry leak testing at 150 psi for AI liquid cooling manifolds.

book_subsections.title: Inside Segment 1 & 2: Defense Electronics vs. Airframe Engineering
paragraphs: To see how AXISCADES earns its money on the ground, walk through two real-world customer deployments side by side. Start on India's northern borders, where the Indian Army faces a persistent asymmetric threat: low-cost commercial drones and loitering munitions flying beneath conventional air-defense radar horizons. Mistral Solutions engineers an autonomous Counter-UAS defense shield for precisely this battlefield problem. A mast-mounted 3D MIMO radar picks up micro-Doppler reflections from spinning plastic propellers at five kilometers; passive radio-frequency antennas locate the operator's 2.4 GHz or 5.8 GHz control signal; cooled thermal cameras slew onto the target; an onboard neural network separates hostile drones from birds in under two seconds; and smart directional jammers sever command and GPS links so the drone drops harmlessly. Priced between ₹3.5 crores and ₹7.5 crores per unit with roughly 45% gross margins across hardware, AI software, and multi-year maintenance, this is proprietary defense technology—not hourly labor.

Now compare that with Segment 2: Aerospace Systems. When a European airline decides to retrofit an Airbus A321neo cabin for higher passenger density, it cannot simply bolt extra seats onto the cabin floor. Shifting seat rows changes the aircraft's center of gravity and emergency floor load paths under 16g forward crash-deceleration rules mandated by EASA CS-25 and FAA FAR-25. AXISCADES' structural stress engineers run finite element models in NASTRAN and PATRAN to redesign lightweight aluminum-lithium underfloor brackets while holding a structural safety margin above 1.25. While the pure-play staffing portion of aerospace engineering is transitioning under the 51%/49% Akkodis transaction, AXISCADES retains specialized aero-tooling, electrical wiring interconnect engineering, and high-value airworthiness integration.

book_subsections.title: Inside Segment 3 & 4: AI Liquid Cooling & Satellite Hardware
paragraphs: The final two segments demonstrate where the Akkodis proceeds are being pointed. In Segment 3—Advanced Precision Manufacturing and Semiconductor Infrastructure—AXISCADES acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru's Cloud Wave Technologies (₹260 crore enterprise value) alongside Silicon Valley subsidiary XiDA Inc. (incorporating ITSJ Group). Why does an Indian aerospace engineer want to machine copper plates for US data centers? Because next-generation AI server processors dissipate 700 to 1,200 watts of concentrated heat, rendering traditional air-fan cooling thermodynamically obsolete. Cloud Wave uses 5-axis CNC machines to mill 50-micron fluid microchannels into oxygen-free copper cold plates flat to within 5 microns, vacuum-brazes them into zero-drip stainless steel manifolds, and pressure-tests every unit with helium mass spectrometry at 150 psi before shipping to US AI rack integrators at $12,000 to $18,000 per compute rack.

Finally, in Segment 4—Space and Satellite Subsystems via Xponential Space and partners like U-Space—AXISCADES fabricates octagonal carbon-fiber composite satellite buses and shape-memory-alloy solar array release mechanisms for 150-kilogram Low Earth Orbit earth-observation satellites. Built to survive 12g rocket launch acoustics and orbital swings from -120°C to +130°C, these spacecraft bus kits command ₹2.5 crores to ₹4.5 crores per unit at 20%+ operating margins. Taken together, Q1 FY27 continuing revenue surging 94% YoY to ₹183.4 crores confirms that this product-centric core is rapidly overtaking the legacy staffing shell.
